procedural_matters: Original hearing
Hearing No. 46 was heard together with Hearings No. 50 and 57 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b), since all hearings arose from the same incident.
HKG 2840 was represented by Alfred Yib.
IRL 3157 was represented by Louise Hanley.
Michalina Wroblewska and Stavros Kouris, members of the international jury, gave evidence.
HKG 2840 provided photo evidence.
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
Reopened hearing
The international jury decided that new evidence became available within a reasonable time and reopened Hearings No. 46, 50 and 57 on 9 July in accordance with RRS 63.7(a)(3), see Case 67.
The parties were present.
The majority of the panel were members of the original committee in accordance with RRS 63.7(c)(1), and Chris Atkins replaced Niclas Kath.
Hearing No. 46 was heard together with Hearings No. 50, 57 and 66 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b), since all hearings arose from the same incident.
HKG 2840 was represented by Alfred Yib.
IRL 3157 was represented by Louise Hanley.
HUN 3306 was represented by Barnabas Gereben.
SLO 3301 was represented by Lana Al-Dilaimi.
USA 3384 was represented by Alexandra Fisher.
Michalina Wroblewska, a member of the international jury, gave evidence as a witness.
HKG 2840 provided photo evidence of the damage.
The international jury provided video evidence of the incident.
Juliet Ryhn, Alex Hon (HKG 2840's helm), Mark Magyar (HUN 3306's crew), Lauren O'Callaghan (USA 3384's coach), and John Tse (HKG 2840's coach) attended the hearing as observers.
facts: Original hearing:
F2 Purple fleet, wind conditions were 18–20 knots with chop.
HKG 2840 approached mark 2s on a reaching starboard-tack course.
IRL 3157 was approaching mark 2s on a port-tack reaching course below the port layline.
IRL 3157 entered the zone of mark 2s overlapped inside an unidentified boat with a red gennaker.
HKG 2840 started rounding mark 2s.
IRL 3157 dropped her gennaker.
HKG 2840 luffed to a beam reach. At that moment, there was another boat clear ahead of HKG 2840 by less than one boat length.
The unidentified boat sailed to windward of mark 2s and close to it. IRL 3157 sailed to leeward of mark 2s.
There was contact between the bow of IRL 3157 and the starboard hull side of HKG 2840.
The contact resulted in a hole below the gunwale on the starboard side of HKG 2840, approximately 20 cm in diameter and 1.5 m from the stern, with additional cracks on the top side of the hull.
HKG 2840 was taking in water.
IRL 3157 took a Two-Turn Penalty.
HKG 2840 retired from race F2 and did not start race F3.
Reopened hearing:
F2 Purple fleet, wind conditions were 18–20 knots with chop.

Four boats were approaching mark 2s overlapped when the first of them reached the zone. IRL 3157 was on port tack and inside, followed by HUN 3306 on port tack, SLO 3301 on starboard tack, and HKG 2840 on starboard tack and on the outside.
There was insufficient room for IRL 3157, HUN 3306 and SLO 3301 all to sail to the mark inside HKG 2840.
As a result, IRL 3157 passed the wrong side of the mark and collided with HKG 2840, which was the first boat to round the mark.
IRL 3157 was unable to avoid the contact because of the surrounding boats.
HKG 2840 suffered serious damage, including a holed hull, retired from race F2 and did not start race F3.
conclusions: The unidentified boat outside overlapped at the zone failed to give IRL 3157 mark-room and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
The unidentified boat caused contact between IRL 3157 and HKG 2840 even though it was reasonably possible to avoid causing it, and broke RRS 14(b).
IRL 3157, on port tack, failed to keep clear of HKG 2840, on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
Since IRL 3157 was compelled to break RRS 10 as a consequence of an unidentified boat breaking RRS 18.2(a)(1), she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breach.
It was not reasonably possible for IRL 3157 to avoid contact with HKG 2840. IRL 3157 did not break RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for HKG 2840, the right-of-way boat, to avoid contact with IRL 3157 when it became clear that IRL 3157 was not keeping clear. HKG 2840 did not break RRS 14(a).

HKG 2840's places in races F2 and F3 were made significantly worse through no fault of her own by physical damage caused by the action of an unidentified boat that was breaking RRS 18.2(a)(1). However, the unidentified boat was neither penalized nor took an applicable penalty. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(2) were not met.
HKG 2840 failed to give mark-room to all boats overlapped inside her at the zone and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
HKG 2840 failed to avoid contact when required to give mark-room and therefore broke RRS 14(a).
HKG 2840 is not entitled to redress because she was required to retire under RRS 44.1(b), which she did. HKG 2840 took an applicable penalty.
IRL 3157 broke RRS 10 but is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a), and did not break RRS 14(a), as it was not reasonably possible for her to avoid contact.
SLO 3301 broke RRS 18.2(a)(1) with respect to HUN 3306 and IRL 3157, but is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a), as she was compelled to do so by HKG 2840's breach of RRS 18.2(a)(1).
HUN 3306 broke RRS 18.2(a)(1) with respect to IRL 3157, but is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a), as she was compelled to do so by SLO 3301's breach of RRS 18.2(a)(1).
decision: The protest is dismissed, since IRL 3157 is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for her breach.
Redress is not given to HKG 2840.
